title: Affine quotient of a finite locally free relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes over $S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $s,t:R\to U$ be finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Suppose $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $R(H)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(H)$ for every $S$-scheme $H$. Put $C=\{a\in A:s^\sharp(a)=t^\sharp(a)\}$, a subring of $A$. Then $M=\operatorname{Spec}C$ represents the fppf sheafification [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $H\mapsto U(H)/R(H)$. The canonical map $U\to M$ is finite locally free and surjective, $R\cong U\times_MU$ compatibly with the projections, and $M$ has the unique $S$-structure making $U\to M$ a morphism over $S$.

proof.text: An equivalence relation on all $S$-valued test schemes supplies identity, inverse and composition uniquely: send $u$ to $(u,u)$, reverse $(u,v)$, and send a composable pair $(u,v),(v,w)$ to $(u,w)$. These operations are natural; full faithfulness of Yoneda turns them into morphisms, and equality on all test points proves the groupoid laws. They also give a groupoid on arbitrary test schemes by considering each possible structure map to $S$. Write $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp$. Since they agree on $C$, the canonical map $q:U\to M=\operatorname{Spec}C$ equalizes $s,t$. The affine fibre-product formula gives $U\times_M U=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_C A)$, and the comparison is induced by $\phi(a\otimes a_2)=\sigma(a)\tau(a_2)$. If $A=0$, the maps $A\to B$ force $B=C=0$; all schemes concerned are empty and the assertions follow. Henceforth $A\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 03BM, first paragraph, and the equivalence-relation groupoid operations

proof.text: The comparison $k:R\to U\times_MU$ is a monomorphism: equality after its two projections implies equality after $j$, and the hypothesis on $H$-points gives equality of the original maps. It is finite: a finite list generating $B$ over $A$ via $\sigma$ also generates it over $A\otimes_C A$ via $\phi$, because this larger scalar action includes $\sigma(A)$. The finite-monomorphism lemma makes $k$ a closed immersion. On these affine schemes this means exactly that $\phi$ is surjective.

Apply the invariant-ring integrality and orbit lemmas to the groupoid just constructed. Thus $A$ is integral over $C$, $q$ is surjective, and the fibres of $|U|\to|M|$ are the $R$-orbits. These statements apply also to every affine groupoid obtained below after changing the invariant base.

source.place: Tag 03BM, second and final paragraphs, using Tags 03BJ and 03BL

proof.text: For a flat $C$-algebra $D$, tensor the exact sequence $0\to C\to A\xrightarrow{\tau-\sigma} B$ with $D$. Flat tensor exactness identifies $D$ with the equalizer in $A_D=A\otimes_C D$ of $\sigma_D,\tau_D:A_D\to B_D=B\otimes_C D$. The operations base change because they are over $M$ (the two maps to $M$ coincide); all groupoid equations remain equations after base change. Thus the new invariant ring is exactly $D$.

For each prime $\mathfrak p\subset C$, apply the flat local extension lemma to $C_{\mathfrak p}$ and the infinite field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)(z)$. It gives a flat local map $C_{\mathfrak p}\to D$ with infinite residue field. This local map is faithfully flat. Localization is flat, so apply the preceding equalizer argument first to $C\to C_{\mathfrak p}$ and then to $C_{\mathfrak p}\to D$. We will prove $A_D$ finite free over $D$ and $\phi_D$ an isomorphism for each such choice.

source.place: Tag 03BM, second and fourth paragraphs; Algebra Tag 03C3

proof.text: For $s:R\to U$, and likewise $t$, finite-flat-lfp pushforward is finite locally free. On affine schemes this supplies a cover by principal opens with $B$ finite free over $A$ via the chosen map; choose a finite such cover since $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is quasi-compact. Tensoring each displayed basis with $A_D$ gives the same kind of principal-open free cover for $B_D$ over $A_D$. The finite-free algebra spectrum lemma on each member proves $s_D,t_D$ finite locally free. In particular these maps have finite fibres. These affine basis descriptions will also be used when returning to $C$.

source.place: Tag 02KB (morphisms-lemma-finite-flat), affine calculation, and base change of an explicit basis

proof.text: Work now over the local invariant ring $(D,\mathfrak m)$ and abbreviate $A_D,B_D$ by $A,B$. By integrality, every maximal ideal of $A$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$, and every prime of $A$ above $\mathfrak m$ is maximal. There is such a point $u_0$ by surjectivity of the orbit lemma. Every other maximal point lies in its $R$-orbit and is therefore in $t(s^{-1}(u_0))$. The fibre $s^{-1}(u_0)$ is finite, so $A$ is semilocal. Also $\mathfrak m A$ lies in every maximal ideal of $A$, hence in its Jacobson radical.

The degree function of $s$ is locally constant. Its values at $s(r)$ and $t(r)$ are equal: composition with the arrow $r$ and its inverse identifies the source fibres after extension to $\kappa(r)$, and fibre degree is unchanged by that extension. All maximal points of $A$ are in one orbit by the preceding step, hence have the same degree $r$. Every prime is contained in a maximal ideal, and a locally constant function takes equal values at two points in a specialization chain; therefore this degree is $r$ everywhere. The identity section makes $s$ surjective, so $r\geq1$. The module $B$ via $\sigma$ is consequently finite locally free of constant rank $r$.

source.place: Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), fibre-isomorphism argument, used in Tag 03BM

proof.text: Apply the semilocal submodule basis lemma to $D\to A$, $P=B$ via $\sigma$, and $N=\tau(A)$. This is a $D$-submodule because $D$ consists of invariants. Surjectivity of $\phi$ says precisely that $N$ spans $B$ over $A$. The residue field is infinite, $A$ is semilocal, $\mathfrak m A\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$, and $B$ has the required constant positive rank by the preceding steps. We obtain $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in A$ such that $\tau(x_j)$ form an $A$-basis of $B$. The affine groupoid basis-descent lemma then gives $A=\bigoplus_j D x_j$ and identifies $\phi_D:A\otimes_D A\to B$ with an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03BM, final paragraph, second half; Algebra Tag 03C1 and Groupoids Tag 03C8

proof.text: Return to the original $C,A,B$. For each $\mathfrak p$, faithful flatness of $C_{\mathfrak p}\to D$ detects exactness, so $\phi_{\mathfrak p}$ is an isomorphism, since $\phi_D$ is. The flatness descent lemma likewise gives that $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $C_{\mathfrak p}$. A module vanishing at every prime is zero: a nonzero element has proper annihilator, contained in a maximal ideal where its localization is still nonzero. Apply this test to the kernel and cokernel of $\phi$ to conclude that $\phi$ is an isomorphism. For any injection $L\to L_2$, localization exactness makes $L_{\mathfrak p}\to L_2_{\mathfrak p}$ injective, and flatness of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ gives injectivity after tensoring. The same zero test on its kernel shows $L\otimes_C A\to L_2\otimes_C A$ injective. Thus $A$ is flat over $C$.

source.place: Tag 03BM, second paragraph, descent of the comparison and flatness

proof.text: Since $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is surjective and flat, $C\to A$ is faithfully flat. The finite principal-open free cover of $B$ over $A$ from step 6 shows that $B$ is a finitely presented $A$-module. Under $\phi$, this is $A\otimes_C A$ with the $A$-action on its first factor. Faithfully flat descent of finite presentation, applied to the $C$-module $A$, makes $A$ finitely presented over $C$.

source.place: Tag 03BM, second paragraph, finite-presentation descent using Algebra Tag 03C4

proof.text: By steps 10 and 11, $A$ is a flat and finitely presented $C$-module, so the finitely-presented flat projectivity lemma makes $A$ a finite projective $C$-module. A finite projective module has a finite principal-open free cover: there are $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in C$ generating the unit ideal with each $A_{g_i}$ finite free over $C_{g_i}$. By the affine fibre-product formula the preimage of $D(g_i)$ in $U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A_{g_i}$, and the finite-free algebra spectrum lemma shows that $\operatorname{Spec}A_{g_i}\to\operatorname{Spec}C_{g_i}$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. Flatness at a point is a condition on local rings, and finite presentation at a point asks for affine neighbourhoods of the point and of its image; every point of $U$ lies over some open $D(g_i)$, so $q$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. For finiteness, let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq M$ be an affine open. The affine fibre-product formula gives $q^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_CR)$, and the images of finitely many $C$-module generators of $A$ generate $A\otimes_CR$ as an $R$-module. Hence $q$ is finite locally free. Surjectivity was already proved in step 3, and the affine fibre-product formula together with $\phi$ gives $R\cong U\times_MU$ with exactly the original projections.

source.place: Tag 03BM, second paragraph, last sentence ('Hence A is finite locally free over C, see Algebra, Lemma 00NX'), and comparison conclusion

proof.text: The finite locally free surjection $q$ is an fppf cover. It is also a singleton fpqc cover, since its inverse image of each affine open is affine, flat and surjective. The maps $U\to S$ agree on $R=U\times_MU$, so fpqc descent of scheme morphisms gives a unique map $M\to S$ making $q$ an $S$-morphism. Every fppf covering is an fpqc covering: its maps are open by flat-lfp openness, and the images of affine opens inside the inverse image of an affine open $V$ form an open cover of $V$; quasi-compactness selects finitely many of them, as required in the fpqc definition. Thus representable fpqc descent makes $h_M$ an fppf sheaf. On the fppf site over $S$, every $H\to M$ lifts after the fppf covering $H\times_MU\to H$, by base-change stability of fppf coverings. If two elements of $U(H)$ have the same image in $M(H)$, their pair is an $H$-point of $U\times_MU=R$, so their quotient classes are equal. The quotient presheaf therefore maps injectively and locally surjectively to $h_M$. The local-bijection sheafification criterion identifies its associated sheaf with $h_M$.

source.place: Tag 03BM, first paragraph via Tag 03C5 (groupoids-lemma-criterion-quotient-representable); descent of the S-structure

lean.statement: theorem finiteFlat_affineRelation_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} {A B : CommRingCat.{u}} (a : Spec A ⟶ S) (b : Spec B ⟶ S) (s t : Over.mk b ⟶ Over.mk a) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] [s.left.IsFiniteLocallyFree] [t.left.IsFiniteLocallyFree] (hrel : ∀ H : Over S, Equivalence (fun x y : H ⟶ Over.mk a ↦ ∃ r : H ⟶ Over.mk b, r ≫ s = x ∧ r ≫ t = y)) : (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left).IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧ Surjective (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left) ∧ (∃ e : Spec B ≅ pullback (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left) (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left), e.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = s.left ∧ e.hom ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = t.left) ∧ ∃ m : Spec (CommRingCat.of (affineRelationInvariants s.left t.left)) ⟶ S, ∃ hq : affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left ≫ m = a, (∀ m' : Spec (CommRingCat.of (affineRelationInvariants s.left t.left)) ⟶ S, affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left ≫ m' = a → m' = m) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (yoneda.obj (Over.mk m)) ∧ ∃ η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk m), coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η = yoneda.map (Over.homMk (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left) hq) ∧ ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : yoneda.obj (Over.mk m) ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ k)
lean.note: The two helper definitions specialize RingHom.eqLocus to Spec.homEquiv and take Spec of its subtype inclusion. The quotient presheaf is the Yoneda coequalizer, and its sheafification is expressed by the universal property of the canonical unit, without assuming sheafification of all Type u-valued presheaves on the big site.
